sources.headline: Amazon Raises U.S. Employee Pay To $20/Hour; Adds Banking And Grocery Benefits
ROUNDUP/Aktien New York Schluss: Deutliche Gewinne mit weiterem Ölpreisrückgang
Amazon Plans Major Expansion Of Same-Day Delivery Network To Challenge Walmart

summary.long:
The main share-price driver is a **major order worth up to $8 billion**: Generac is supplying Amazon with generators to secure its data centers, and there is also an **option for an equity stake by Amazon in Generac**. This strengthens the infrastructure for AWS and AI applications and was rewarded on the stock market with price gains for both companies.

Previously, Amazon had outlined with **“Project Mercury”** the massive expansion of its same-day delivery network in the US. By 2031, **over 1,000 local warehouses** are to be built, holding around 90,000 fast-moving items and bringing Prime customers closer to the goods. Internally, **$6.8 billion of investments** are planned for this in 2026 and 2027.

In parallel, Amazon is increasing the **starting wage in US logistics jobs to $20 per hour** and introducing new financial and food benefits. This improves its attractiveness as an employer, but also means higher personnel costs in its US core business.
summary.short: A major emergency power order for Generac is supporting Amazon’s cloud expansion and fueling speculation about a possible equity participation, while the group is simultaneously massively expanding its same-day logistics.
